verification_evidence.revised_phrasing_assessment: The revised qualitative phrasing adequately supports the hardcoded-Exhibit-A argument. The load-bearing claim is structural (r=0.992 and AI=1.152 are hardcoded HTML with no computation anywhere in the dome repository — corroborated by curmudgeon WIN-011.c3 dome_code_analysis); the spurious-correlation paragraph is supporting context, and converting it from an unsupported quantitative assertion (Monte Carlo/37%) to an accurate qualitative one removes the tu-quoque exposure without weakening the structural argument. The corrected physical mechanism (atmospheric/ionospheric storm-time loading rather than direct nT-scale EM forcing on SGs) is accurate: superconducting gravimeters respond to mass redistribution and loading, not to magnetic-field perturbations per se.
verification_evidence.citation_gap: The claim that high correlation between two autocorrelated geophysical time series under a shared driver is statistically unremarkable is textbook, but currently uncited. Canonical sources: Yule (1926) J. Roy. Stat. Soc. 89(1):1-63, "Why do we sometimes get nonsense-correlations between time-series?" — the founding treatment of spurious correlation between autocorrelated series; Granger & Newbold (1974) J. Econometrics 2:111-120, "Spurious regressions in econometrics". Citing these closes the residual "says who?" hole the decider flagged in the attention item.
